subjective.citation_text: Patient: I'm 38 years old, and I'm a female. I'm here because I've been having really bad acid reflux, and my primary doctor referred me. Doctor: Could you please describe when your acid reflux symptoms started and what they feel like? Patient: I've had acid reflux since I was around 12, but it's gotten worse over the past few years. It feels like a burning sensation in my chest and throat, and some days it's really bad, especially after eating certain things. Doctor: Could you describe the specific foods or activities that trigger your acid reflux episodes, and have you experienced any associated symptoms such as regurgitation, difficulty swallowing, or unintended weight loss? Patient: I don't have any difficulty swallowing, and I haven't lost any weight unintentionally. As for triggers, spicy foods, soda, and sometimes even citrus or tomato-based foods seem to make it worse. Stress at work also seems to play a role. Doctor: Have you been diagnosed with GERD or any other gastrointestinal condition in the past? If so, what treatments have you received, and how effective were they? Patient: I don't think I've ever been officially diagnosed with GERD, but I've been dealing with acid reflux for a long time. I was on omeprazole for about a year, and it helped some days but not others. I also tried ranitidine at one point, and that helped too, but I haven't been on anything else. Doctor: Has the patient undergone any endoscopic evaluation of the upper gastrointestinal tract, such as an esophagogastroduodenoscopy (EGD), to assess for structural abnormalities or complications of chronic acid reflux? Patient: I don't think I've had an upper endoscopy in the last 10 years, maybe when I was younger, but I can't remember for sure. Doctor: Has the patient ever had an upper endoscopy at any point in her life, even if it was many years ago? Patient: Yes, I think I had one when I was
